plan_draft.title: Data Analytics App with NumPy
plan_draft.overview: Set up a Python project that uses NumPy 2.5.0 for array creation, random sampling, and basic analytics. Provide a runnable script demonstrating these capabilities and include Pydantic as an additional dependency.

phases.title: Project Initialization
phases.body:
- Create a directory `analytics_app`.
- Initialize a Git repository.
- Run `python -m venv venv` to create a virtual environment.
- Activate the venv and install NumPy 2.5.0 with `pip install "numpy==2.5.0"`[^numpy-1].
- Add a `.gitignore` that excludes `venv/` and `__pycache__/`.

phases.title: Core Script Structure
phases.body:
- Create `main.py` and add `import numpy as np`[^numpy-2].
- Define `generate_data()` that returns `np.arange(15, dtype=np.int64).reshape(3,5)`[^numpy-2].
- Define `sample_normal()` that returns `np.random.default_rng().normal(size=2500)`[^numpy-2].
- Define `compute_stats(arr)` that returns `arr.max(axis=1)`[^numpy-2].
- Add an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block that calls the three functions and prints their results.

phases.title: Uvicorn Integration
phases.body:
- Add `uvicorn` to the `dependencies` list in `pyproject.toml`.
- Install uvicorn in the virtual environment with `pip install "uvicorn"`.
- Create a placeholder `server.py` that will import the FastAPI app (to be added later) and run it with uvicorn (implementation pending due to lack of library brief).
- Document in `README.md` how to start the server with `uvicorn server:app --reload` (note: exact command may need adjustment once FastAPI is integrated).
- Ensure the project still runs existing scripts after adding the dependency.

phases.title: Pydantic Integration
phases.body:
- Add `pydantic` to the `dependencies` list in `pyproject.toml`.
- Install pydantic in the virtual environment with `pip install "pydantic"`.
- Create `models.py` as a placeholder for future Pydantic models.
- Document that specific model definitions are pending due to lack of library brief.
- Ensure the project still runs the existing scripts after adding the dependency.

phases.title: Verification Script
phases.body:
- Create `verify.py`.
- Import the functions from `main.py`.
- Assert `generate_data().shape == (3,5)`.
- Assert `compute_stats(generate_data()).shape == (3,)`.
- Assert `sample_normal().shape == (2500,)`.
- Print "All checks passed" if no assertion fails.

phases.title: Documentation
phases.body:
- Write `README.md` with usage instructions.
- Include a code snippet showing `np.arange`, `np.random.Generator.normal`, and `ndarray.max` with citations[^numpy-2].
- Document how to activate the venv and run `python main.py`.
- Explain the purpose of each function.
- Add a section on reproducible random sampling (seed the generator).

phases.title: Packaging Configuration
phases.body:
- Add a `pyproject.toml` with `[project]` metadata.
- Specify `numpy = "==2.5.0"` in the `dependencies` list[^numpy-1].
- Ensure the project builds with `python -m pip install .`.
- Include `scripts = {analytics="analytics_app.main:main"}` if desired.
- Commit all files to Git.
- Tag the initial release as `v0.1.0`.

phases.title: Final Validation
phases.body:
- Activate the virtual environment.
- Run `python -m pip install -e .` to install the package in editable mode.
- Execute `python main.py` and verify printed results.
- Run `python verify.py` and confirm it exits without error.
- Run `python -m pip uninstall -y numpy && pip install "numpy==2.5.0"` to test reinstallability.
- Document any observed issues in `README.md`.

pitfalls: NumPy 2.5.0 requires Python 3.9+; using an older interpreter will fail[^numpy-1].
Mixing incompatible dtypes (e.g., int64 with float32) can trigger implicit upcasting or loss of precision[^numpy-2].
Broadcasting requires shape compatibility; operations on arrays with mismatched dimensions raise a ValueError[^numpy-2].
Calling `np.random.default_rng()` repeatedly creates independent generators; seed once and reuse for reproducibility[^numpy-2].
Very large arrays can exhaust memory; keep sample sizes reasonable for the target environment.
If the virtual environment is not activated, `pip install` may affect the global Python environment.
